items.editor_note: Sets the thesis: agent reliability and efficiency come from reasoning structure, not just model size.

items.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
items.summary_1line: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated....
items.editor_note: Extends efficiency to diffusion language agents by adapting compute placement and generation length.

editorial.tldr: On Oct 22 an arXiv agent-systems paper argued that reliable multi-turn agents need better structured reasoning, not just bigger models. Five days later two papers moved the efficiency question into serving mechanics.
editorial.whats_new: Two Oct 27 arXiv papers target inference cost directly: CRISP prunes and schedules MoE experts for edge servers, and Metacognitive Decoding tunes diffusion-LM agents' compute and output length.
editorial.why_it_matters: Inference cost for agents is being attacked at the serving layer (expert-weight movement, decoding length), which affects hardware sizing and latency budgets more than model choice alone.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: if you serve MoE models on edge or memory-limited hosts, profile expert-weight movement before sizing hardware, and wait for released code before changing a serving stack.

status.detail: Three research papers, no production releases yet; the thread is about techniques, not shipped tooling.

beats.headline: Reliability through structure, not scale
beats.summary: A paper argues multi-turn agents need structure-grounded reasoning rather than larger models.

beats.headline: Two techniques cut serving cost for MoE and diffusion agents
beats.summary: CRISP targets expert-weight movement on memory-constrained edge servers; Metacognitive Decoding adapts where compute goes and how much text diffusion LMs generate.

open_questions: Do CRISP or Metacognitive Decoding release code or serving-framework integrations?
Do independent benchmarks reproduce the efficiency gains the authors report?
Does diffusion-LM decoding show up in any production agent runtime?
